questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have previously traveled in Latin America, and since I study spanish language and culture it made great sense to go back here.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not too easy. I had to contact the supervisor various times, before she got back to me. Since there was a delay in the application process that I had not been informed about, It was pretty stressful at first, cause I had to insist on getting the information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was 3 introduction days for all exchange students at Uniandes, and we could contact an employee at the uni, who always replied fast.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: There was a lot of information, which I understand is necessary to some extent, but some of the info felt irrelevant, like e.g. the presentation about the security system on campus.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
To me it was extremely easy cause I already have Latin American friends. But in general it should be easy for anyone in Bogota, and there are also facebook groups you can join, like the group "Housing"
https://www.facebook.com/groups/414493191922940

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's way better than living on campus, that is what everyone says. In cityU (the on-campus residence) it's very expensive, and you don't have anything - so you have to go buy everything from cuttlery to pillows. And there are a ton of rules there (no smoking, no drinking etc.) When you live off campus you have so much more freedom, and you can either have your own studio or live in a big house with other students. Plus you can get tolive with locals, which in my opinion is much more interesting that living with other foreigners.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was pretty stressful because you get told on beforehand that you have to be ready cause there at limited spots. However I got all the courses I wanted and more.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The same employee who was available at all the time responded within minutes to any e-mail.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do good research about the classes and take advantage of the fact that you can create "wish-schedules" before registering. Because you have to figure out yourself which classes you can take that don't overlap, the system will just reject you if you apply for to classes at the same time. I had 4 different templates of schedules, and itreally helped me get an overview.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I studied art, painting and drawing, so I didn't have a lot of academic experiences like that in Uniandes.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: My courses where interesting and challenging, I really improved my painting and drawing skills and learned a lot. Sometimes it was challenging since I don't normally study art, but the professors were really helpful. If you don't speak good spanish it could be a really big challenge, I'm fluent and I often misunderstood assignments.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It's very different from the danish university. There are many test and many assignments. Much more like Gymnasie than university, so it can feel like much more work, in some ways.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Painting bodies
Basic painting
Basic drawing
Drawing space

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you are artistic, this is an amazing opportunity for you. I got to spend 5 months painting and drawing and the facilities at Uniandes' art department are amazing. You get to learn from professors who all work currently as artists. I really recommend studying art courses here. But there are a bunch of materials that you have to buy, so it's a bit more expensive, but totally worth it.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Everything is quite cheap in Colombia. Only thing could be that somethings might not be AS cheap as you expect, but it's still cheaper than DK.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Transportation. It's cheap but since you take a lot of cars around you end up spendig more than you might think at first. 
Food delivery is really really cheap though.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't use any non academic facilities at uni.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were sport classes, dance lessons and events for exchange students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't participate in any so I don't know.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go out of the city! There are plenty of lovely villages and places in nature to see. Or book flights to further away in the country - if you do it a few weeks in advance the tickets to e.g. the caribbean coast could be like 300 dkk for the round trip.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It's very different here. To me it was easy cause I adjust well to Latin american culture, since I'm and open person and I speak spanish. You should know that Colombians are much better at small talking than danes, so you can get friends while waiting in line for your lunch.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Don't be shy. Speak spanish with them, and invite them to hang out. Then it's not difficult at all.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
The fact that people in Bogota don't move when you need to get on the Transmilenio (the metro) so you have to push them. 
And the fact that you can't walk in the streets at night.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The heartwarming people. It's very easy to befriend a colombian. And the parties are amazing here, lots of dancing and much better night clubs than in DK.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1 If you want and ID card to access uni, you should start insisting on it early on. I never got mine, and had to enter everyday with my admission-letter. Not a big deal, but still annoying.

2 People in Colombia a usually much younger when they start university (around 16-17 yrs old) So if you're a bit older like me  when you go (26) you might find it challenging to bond with fellow students.

Be patient with the colombian bureaucracy. There are a lot of forms to fill out, and the processes are slower than we are used to in DK.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Bogota can be pretty cold, and none of the houses are isolated. So bring warm socks and sweaters for the nights. 
And it also rains, but so much that you just use an umbrella, so no need to bring all your danish rain-gear.
Some people bike, but the distances are way longer that in CPH and the traffic is like freeways (pretty crazy) in many places, so I don't recommend it. 
Always have cash on you, but not too much.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I got a bunch of great friends that I will always want to come back to and visit.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Sometimes it's hard to be so far away from your family.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Don't let you scare away from people saying that Colombia is dangerous. Just don't be irresponsible and have fun, Bogota is an incredible city!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
